about: Every character a record, a rank file or a species' spec may state (growth plan G2.2, and the characters of the spec rework): its group, the organ it describes, its type and its unit, values or range. Vocabulary only: the rules that turn characters into spec values live in the taxa they hold for. Types: number (a quantity in its unit), count (a whole number), bool, enum (one of its values), enums (a list of its values), months (a list of months, 1 to 12), colour (sRGB, three numbers 0 to 255), text (a line in PlantGen's own words), ids (species ids). A number or count may instead be a range, {"min": 5, "max": 8}, with the rare extremes beyond it as `low` and `high` and the most usual value as `typical`: a flora's (3-)5-8 is {"min": 5, "max": 8, "low": 3}. A range says how the plant varies, not how sure a source is. An enum or bool may instead be qualified, each state with how often it occurs (usually, often, sometimes, rarely): usually opposite, rarely alternate is {"opposite": "usually", "alternate": "rarely"}. Organs are the parts characters describe, the whole plant, a tissue such as bark and a group such as an inflorescence among them, so far those of vascular plants; each but the plant is part of another. An organ with a `when` exists only where one of those characters takes one of the values listed (a qualified value counts with each of its states), and its characters apply only there; a character's own `when` narrows it further, as leaves_per_whorl applies only to whorled leaves. A character marked `optional` is one many plants have nothing to state for, and the audit never counts it missing.

plant.why: the whole plant: its form, size, life and where it grows

root.why: what grows underground to anchor the plant and take up water

stem.why: the shoots that bear leaves, flowers and cones, and the wood they lay down

bark.why: the outer layer of a woody stem

leaf.why: a leaf from its stalk to its tip; a fern's frond and a grass's blade are leaves

leaflet.why: one of the separate blades of a compound leaf

inflorescence.why: a flowering shoot: how flowers, heads or spikelets are grouped

flower.why: a single flower, where single flowers make up the inflorescence

capitulum.why: a head: florets packed on a shared receptacle inside a ring of bracts (phyllaries), as in the daisy family

ray_floret.why: a floret at the rim of a radiate head, its corolla drawn out into a strap (lamina)

disc_floret.why: a floret in the middle of a head, its corolla a small tube

ligulate_floret.why: a floret of a head made only of strap-shaped florets, as in dandelions

spikelet.why: the unit of grasses and sedges: florets on a small axis, in grasses above a pair of glumes

fruit.why: a ripe fruit, from a flower or floret

library_form.why: Library 1.0's nine classes, for search and its quotas per class

growth_form.why: the spec's growth forms, which pick a rank file's part for its form

reproduction.why: how it bears seeds or spores: seeds in fruit from flowers, seeds open on the scales of cones, seeds borne singly or in pairs outside any cone (yews, ginkgo), or spores and no seeds

leaf_habit.why: how long leaves stay on through the year

life_span.why: how many years a plant lives and sets seed in

clonal.why: whether it spreads by its own shoots, runners or roots

habit_notes.why: what the other form traits leave unsaid

crown_width_max_m.why: the widest a crown or clump grows

stem_diameter_max_m.why: the thickest a stem grows, at breast height for trees

branching.why: the crown's habit: a leading stem, a spreading one, a column, canes or none

bark_texture.why: the bark of a grown stem

bark_colour.why: the bark of a grown stem

spines.why: what a plant is armed with: spines from areoles, thorns from shoots, prickles from bark, or spines on its leaves

leaf_form.why: what a leaf is made as: a flat blade (a fern's frond and a grass's leaf among them), a needle or a scale

leaf_division.why: whether the blade is one piece, however deeply cut, or made of separate leaflets

leaf_incision.why: how deeply a simple blade is cut: not at all, into lobes, to about halfway, most of the way, or into fine segments

division_pattern.why: how a compound leaf's leaflets or a cut blade's lobes are set: along a midrib, or from one point

division_order.why: how many times the leaflets or lobes divide: 1 once (pinnate), 2 twice (bipinnate)

leaf_shape.why: a blade's outline, or a compound leaf's leaflets'

leaf_venation.why: how the main veins run: from a midrib, from the base, side by side, forking in pairs, or one vein alone

leaf_arrangement.why: leaves at each node: one (alternate), a pair (opposite) or three or more (whorled)

leaves_per_whorl.why: leaves at each node of a whorled shoot

phyllotaxis_pattern.why: how each leaf node turns from the last: by about the golden angle (spiral), half a turn (distichous, two ranks), a third of a turn (tristichous, three ranks), or half the gap between its own leaves (decussate: pairs crossing, whorls alternating)

divergence_deg.why: the angle between successive leaf nodes, where a source measures it

rosette.why: leaves crowded on short internodes: not at all, at the base, or at the tips of stems

leaf_length_m.why: a grown leaf's blade, without its petiole

leaf_width_m.why: a grown leaf's blade at its widest

petiole_length_m.why: the stalk between blade and shoot

leaf_margin.why: a blade's edge: smooth, or toothed (teeth pointing forward, outward, rounded, or ending in spines)

stipules.why: whether leaves bear stipules at their base

leaf_colour.why: a grown leaf's upper side in summer

inflorescence.why: how the units of a flowering shoot are grouped: L1's cluster kinds, a single unit, or a spadix

inflorescence_unit.why: what an inflorescence is made of: single flowers, heads of florets (the daisy family) or spikelets (grasses and sedges)

units_per_inflorescence.why: the flowers, heads or spikelets in one inflorescence

inflorescence_length_m.why: an inflorescence from its lowest unit or branch to its tip

flower_merosity.why: petals (or tepals) in one whorl of a flower

flower_symmetry.why: a flower's symmetry: radial, one plane, or none

capitulum_kind.why: the florets a head holds: rays round a disc, a disc alone, a disc ringed by threadlike florets, or strap-shaped florets alone

involucre_diameter_m.why: the ring of phyllaries across, which floras give as a head's size

phyllary_series.why: the rows the phyllaries stand in

receptacle.why: whether chaffy scales (paleae) stand among a head's florets

pappus.why: what tops the fruit of a head's florets: nothing, bristles, scales, awns or a small crown

ray_florets.why: the ray florets of one head

disc_florets.why: the disc florets of one head

ligulate_florets.why: the strap-shaped florets of one head

florets_per_spikelet.why: the fertile florets of one spikelet

spikelet_length_m.why: a spikelet from its base to the tip of its last floret, awns left out

glumes.why: the empty bracts at a spikelet's base

awn_length_m.why: the bristle on a floret's lemma, 0 where it has none

sexual_system.why: where the sexes sit: in a dioecious species only half the plants bear fruit or seed cones

fruit_type.why: what a fruit is (pod for dry pods that split other than a legume; cypsela for the achene of the daisy family)

fruit_size_m.why: a ripe fruit at its longest

fruiting_months.why: the months its fruit is ripe in

leaf_out_months.why: the months new leaves unfold in

light.why: the light it grows in, every class it spans

moisture.why: the water its ground holds, every class it spans

soil_texture.why: the ground it roots in, every class it spans

habitat_notes.why: what the other ecology traits leave unsaid

hosts.why: the species a climber, epiphyte or parasite grows on

nurse_forms.why: the forms its seedlings need to shelter under

nurse_species.why: the species its seedlings need to shelter under

litter_kind.why: the ground look its litter makes

self_pruning.why: whether it sheds its own shaded limbs

architectural_model.why: the Halle-Oldeman model its growth follows: a label for search, set by each lineage, never a program

axis_growth.why: whether an axis grows on from its own tip or is carried on by a lateral

flowering_position.why: whether flowers end a shoot or sit beside its leaves

short_shoots.why: whether it grows long shoots and short ones (spurs)

ramification_order.why: branch orders a grown crown carries
